skill.name: ponytail
skill.description: Forces the laziest solution that actually works, simplest, shortest, most minimal. Channels a senior dev who has seen everything: question whether the task needs to exist at all (YAGNI), reach for the standard library before custom code, native platform features before dependencies, one line before fifty. Supports intensity levels: lite, full (default), ultra. Use on ANY coding task: writing, adding, refactoring, fixing, reviewing, or designing code, and choosing libraries or dependencies. Also use whenever the user says "ponytail", "be lazy", "lazy mode", "simplest solution", "minimal solution", "yagni", "do less", or "shortest path", or complains about over-engineering, bloat, boilerplate, or unnecessary dependencies. Do NOT use for non-coding requests (general knowledge, prose, translation, summaries, recipes).
skill.summary: Simplify coding tasks through reuse, standard libraries, native features, and focused checks without removing essential safeguards.
skill.author: dietrichgebert

content.value_statement: Unnecessary abstractions and dependencies make small coding tasks harder to maintain. Ponytail guides your assistant toward existing helpers, standard libraries, and minimal changes while preserving essential safeguards.
actual_capabilities: Prioritizes existing code, standard libraries, native platform features, and installed dependencies before new implementations.
Provides lite, full, and ultra modes for different levels of simplification.
Directs bug fixes toward shared root causes after tracing affected callers.
Documents deliberate simplifications with their limits and upgrade paths.
Requires a runnable check for nontrivial logic while preserving validation, security measures, and accessibility.
Keeps unsolicited explanations short while allowing explicitly requested reports and walkthroughs.
limitations: Provides assistant instructions, not an executable formatter, analyzer, or testing tool.
Applies to coding tasks, not general knowledge, translation, or other non-coding requests.
Does not guarantee correctness, performance, or security; results depend on the assistant and project context.
Prefers one focused check unless broader testing is requested, which may not satisfy a project testing policy.

use_cases.title: Reduce Feature Complexity
use_cases.description: Choose existing helpers or native platform features for a small feature while preserving its required behavior.

use_cases.title: Fix Shared Root Causes
use_cases.description: Trace callers before changing shared logic and add a focused regression check for the reported failure.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Dependency Proposals
use_cases.description: Compare proposed dependencies with standard-library alternatives and document when a more complex implementation becomes necessary.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Simple Approach
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Ponytail lite to review this coding task: [task]. Suggest the simplest alternative without dropping requested behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Implement a Minimal Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Ponytail full to implement [feature] in [project]. Inspect existing helpers first, preserve safeguards, and include a focused runnable check.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: implement a feature with minimal additional code.

prompt_templates.title: Repair a Shared Bug
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Ponytail full to fix [bug]. Trace all callers of [function], repair the shared root cause, and add a regression check.
prompt_templates.scenario: Experienced: fix behavior across multiple call sites.

prompt_templates.title: Challenge a Complex Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Ponytail ultra to simplify [design]. Preserve [requirements], identify unnecessary abstractions, document known limits, and retain the project's required tests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: reassess a design with explicit constraints.

output_examples.input: Review a proposal for a custom date picker using Ponytail lite.
output_examples.output: A native date input may cover the required behavior. Add a custom picker only when specific requirements exceed native capabilities.

output_examples.input: Fix a validation bug shared by several callers using Ponytail full.
output: Place the validation fix in the shared function used by affected callers.
Add a regression check for the failing input.
Avoid duplicating guards in each caller.

output_examples.input: Assess a custom API response cache using Ponytail ultra.
output: Measure the bottleneck before adding a cache.
Consider standard-library caching when its invalidation and freshness behavior meets the requirements.
Use a more specialized cache only when measured needs justify it.

best_practices: State required behavior, security constraints, and project testing rules before requesting simplification.
Inspect existing helpers and trace affected callers before choosing the smallest change.
Document performance limits and upgrade triggers, then run the required correctness checks.
anti_patterns: Remove validation, accessibility, or data-loss protections to shorten code.
Choose the smallest local patch without tracing the shared root cause.
Treat one focused check as sufficient when the project requires broader regression coverage.

faq.question: What does Ponytail do?
faq.answer: It guides coding assistants toward minimal working solutions through reuse, standard libraries, native features, and focused checks.

faq.question: How do the intensity levels differ?
faq.answer: Lite suggests simpler alternatives, full prioritizes minimal implementations, and ultra challenges unnecessary requirements more strongly. Full is the default.

faq.question: Does it allow removing security checks?
faq.answer: No. It explicitly preserves trust-boundary validation, security measures, data-loss protections, accessibility basics, and requested functionality.

faq.question: Does the skill run tools by itself?
faq.answer: No. The reviewed package contains only a Markdown instruction file. Any tool use depends on the host assistant and its permissions.

faq.question: How much testing does it request?
faq.answer: It requests one runnable check for nontrivial logic unless more testing is requested. Existing project testing requirements should still be followed.

faq.question: How can I change or stop the mode?
faq.answer: Select lite, full, or ultra with /ponytail. Say stop ponytail or normal mode to disable it; the selected level otherwise persists.
